units: <cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 16:14">Targ. Gen. XVI, 14</cite>; a. e.

<cite ref="Berakhot 56a:2">Ber. 56ᵃ</cite>. <he>מיבעי עסקך כי הני מידי דנפל לב׳</he> Ms. M., thy goods will be sought for like something fallen into a well (i.e. thy business will thrive; diff. vers. in ed. a. Mss., v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note).
<cite ref="Shabbat 66b:9">Sabb. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>נפל פותא לב׳</he> Dyer’s Madder, as a remedy, has fallen into the pit (is not practiced).
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 92b:2">B. Kam. 92ᵇ</cite> (prov.) <he>ב׳ דשתית וכ׳</he> cast no stone into a well out of which thou once didst drink (never despise what once benefitted you).—
<cite ref="Chullin 106a:8">Ḥull. 106ᵃ</cite> <he>בַּת בֵּירְתָא</he> a little gutter fed by a well.—Pl. <he>בֵּירִין</he>, <cite ref="B00713"><he>בֵּירֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 26:15">Targ. Gen. XXVI, 15</cite>; a. e.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 85a:8">B. Mets. 85ᵃ</cite> <he>ב׳ מליא וכ׳ …</he> the cavity (created by the taking out of a radish) stood full of water; [Ms. M. <he>כי ב׳ דמיא</he> like a well; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note].—Pl. as above.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 14:10">Targ. Gen. XIV, 10</cite> (h. text <he>בֶּאֱרוֹת</he>); <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 42:2">Gen. R. s. 42</cite>.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 7a:10">Snh. 7ᵃ</cite> (prov.) <he>שב ב׳ וכ׳</he> seven pits are open for the righteous man (and he escapes), and one for the evil-doer (into which he falls).

senses.gloss: בֵּירָא pr. n. pl. Bera (prob. ident. with בֵּירַאי 2, a), native place of R. Simlai.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 2:11:3">Y. Taan. II, 65ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>ר׳ ש׳ דיב׳</he>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 1:11:5">Y. Meg. I, 72ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>דב׳</he>; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:14:1">Koh. R. to III, 14</cite> <he>דברויירא</he> (corr. acc.).
